messages:
omar: quick question — noticed route-level flag not overriding project-level in prod. our docs say route should win. anyone seen this?

maya: can you paste the flag payload you pushed?

omar: sure — snippet below (sanitized):
```json
{
  "flag": "new_routing_v2",
  "scopes": [
    {"type": "org", "id": "rw", "value": true},
    {"type": "project", "id": "payments", "value": false},
    {"type": "route", "id": "payments/charge", "value": true}
  ]
}
```

sandra: config looks fine. do you have any caching on the flag eval? sometimes cache keys omit route and you get project-level answer.

omar: we do. redis key format is: `flag:{flag}:{org}:{project}` (i guess route isn't included)

lee: there's the issue. cache key must include scope identifiers present in the flag evaluation (route/model). precedence should be: model > route > project > org (most-specific wins). if a more-specific scope exists, it should override parent scopes.

maya: agreed. also recommend adding an explicit canary guard when a child scope turns a parent-off to on. e.g., if project=false but route=true, require `audience` or `percentage` to avoid full blast.

omar: good call. we had a few users who unexpectedly got the feature after a recent rollout.

devex: action items: 1) change cache key to include route/model where applicable, 2) enforce evaluation order canonicalization, 3) add lint rule to flag configs that have child=true and parent=false without audience. i'll draft docs update.

flagbot: Deploy started: featureflags-service v2.3.1 -> staging :rocket:

sandra: i'll prepare a PR with cache-key fix and unit tests for precedence + cache miss behavior. assign to @maya for code review.

maya: happy to review, assign to me. :thumbsup:

lee: quick note on implementation: prefer deterministic scope tokenization `org|project|route|model` and include present scope ids in key in that order. avoids collisions.

omar: thanks all — timeline? can we target deploy to prod tomorrow morning after small smoke?

sandra: yes, i'll cut the PR today and schedule canary deploy tomorrow 09:00 PST. i'll also add a rollout with 10% audience for routes that flip.

omar: perfect. i'll follow up with a short postmortem doc if anything odd shows up.

devex: i'll update the feature flags doc and the internal checklist for rollout guardrails.

flagbot: Deploy successful: featureflags-service v2.3.1 -> staging (all checks passed).

maya: thanks team.
